questions.q: What are the three endorsement levels in Power BI, in order from lowest to highest?
options: None, Promoted, Certified
Draft, Reviewed, Published
Bronze, Silver, Gold
Private, Shared, Public
questions.explain: Power BI's endorsement system has three levels: None (the default, no signal), Promoted (self-service), and Certified (requires a granted permission).

questions.q: Who can set a dataset or report to 'Promoted'?
options: Only the Power BI tenant administrator
Any owner of that item, directly from its settings
Only a user with the Certified permission
Only Microsoft support
questions.explain: Promoting is self-service — any owner can set it from the item's own settings, with no special permission required.

questions.q: Why is the 'Certified' option grayed out for most users in the endorsement settings?
options: It's a bug that Microsoft hasn't fixed yet
Certified content costs extra in Power BI Premium
Certifying requires a permission an admin has to grant first, since it represents an org-level review
Certified can only be set from Power BI Desktop, not the service
questions.explain: Certification represents an organizational review, not one person's opinion, so it's locked behind a tenant-granted permission rather than being available to every owner.

questions.q: Where do Promoted and Certified badges appear once they're set?
options: Only in the item's own settings page
Only in an email sent to the owner
Wherever the item appears — search results, workspace lists, and the app itself
Only in the Power BI admin portal's audit log
questions.explain: The badges travel with the content everywhere a user might encounter it, so the same trust signal is visible in search results, workspace lists, and apps.

questions.q: What's the core difference in what Promoted versus Certified actually signals to a reader?
options: There's no real difference — they're the same signal with two different names
Promoted means the item is newer; Certified means it's older
Promoted is an owner's own opinion that content is ready; Certified is an org-level review against certification criteria
Promoted applies to reports only; Certified applies to datasets only
questions.explain: Promoted is deliberately a lighter-weight, self-service signal, while Certified represents a reviewed, organizational stamp of approval — that's exactly why one is open to any owner and the other requires a granted permission.
